c.tagline: Palm-fringed Sakalava port on the Mozambique Channel, gateway to the Avenue of the Baobabs.

taxi.fareNote: No ride-hailing apps operate in Morondava. Get around by pousse-pousse (cycle-rickshaw) or tuk-tuk for short hops, and by taxi-brousse (shared bush taxi) for longer trips; nothing is metered, so agree the fare before setting off.

emergency.note: Emergency response outside the main towns is very limited; carry a local SIM and keep your lodge's direct number handy, as private clinics and hotels often arrange transport faster.

avoid.reason: Avoid the beach and unlit streets after dark, when muggings have been reported, and watch belongings in the market.

hood_desc: The sandy peninsula strip where most of Morondava's hotels, restaurants and beach bars line the Mozambique Channel; the natural, walkable base for first-timers, with sunset views and pirogues drawn up on the beach.
The bustling town center around the Bazary Be market, with shops, banks, taxi-brousse departures and everyday Malagasy life; practical and lively rather than scenic.
A Vezo fishing village on the sand spit across the estuary, reached by pirogue, where dugout canoes land the daily catch; a quiet, traditional escape from the hotel strip.
A local residential quarter near the port and river mouth, close to the fishing activity and gare routière; low-key and authentic, handy for onward transport.
A calm inland residential area away from the beach, with local eateries and a slower pace; suits budget travelers wanting an everyday, non-touristy feel.

water.note: Drink bottled or filtered water only; tap water is not potable.

transit.pay: Pousse-pousse and tuk-tuk fares are paid in cash (ariary) and agreed before the ride; long-distance taxi-brousse are paid in cash at the gare routière. There is no transit card.
transit.hours: Pousse-pousse and tuk-tuks run through the day into the early evening; after dark options thin out, so arrange a driver or hotel transfer.
transit.note: Morondava has no bus, tram, or rail network. Short trips around the compact town are by pousse-pousse (cycle-rickshaw) or tuk-tuk; long-distance travel is by taxi-brousse from the gare routiere.

bus: Taxi-brousse (long-distance bush taxis) to Antsirabe, Antananarivo and Belo-sur-Tsiribihina
ferry: Pirogues (dugout canoes) along the coast to Betania and Morombe

transit.m: Private taxi or hotel transfer to the town centre / Nosy Kely (10-15 min)

tip.r: Not obligatory; rounding up or leaving 5-10% for good service in tourist restaurants and for guides and drivers is appreciated but not expected.
